questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which minerals form the typical mafic composition of basalt?
options: Calcite and dolomite with minor quartz characteristic of carbonate rocks
Muscovite, biotite and quartz typical of a felsic plutonic assemblage
Quartz, K-feldspar and plagioclase in roughly equal proportions
questions.solution: Basalt: fine-grained, mafic. Most abundant volcanic rock. Oceanic crust.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Corona texture, seen as reaction rims around minerals, results from which metamorphic process?
options: Incomplete reaction — mineral replacement textures. Olivine rimmed by orthopyroxene + spinel (granulite)
Complete equilibrium melting of the protolith leaving no residual minerals and producing a single homogeneous melt
Eutectic crystallization of the melt into discrete cumulate layers without any post-cumulus reaction
Mechanical mixing of different layers during sedimentary transport forming graded depositional units
questions.solution: Corona: cooling (Opx + Sp around Ol). Kelyphite (Cpx + Sp around Grt). Reaction progress.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which option correctly describes the surface cut by wave erosion at the base of a sea cliff?
options: Steep vertical face of rock that retreats landward under wave attack
Feature formed by deposition of sediment rather than by erosion
Flat, gently sloping surface cut by wave erosion at cliff base
Elevated rock surface that lies permanently above the level of the sea
questions.solution: Platform: erosional. Marine terrace: uplifted platform. Abrasion by sand and pebbles.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Normal mid-ocean ridge basalt (N-MORB) is derived from a depleted mantle source, as shown by what light REE pattern and (La/Sm)_N value?
options: Plume-derived mantle source with high ³He/⁴He and a strong positive Nb anomaly on primitive-mantle normalized diagrams
Enriched mantle source with elevated incompatible element concentrations
Depleted mantle source (light REE depleted). (La/Sm)_N < 1. ~6-8% partial melting of spinel lherzolite
Ocean island basalt source enriched by recycled oceanic crust and sediments
questions.solution: N-MORB: La/Sm < 1. Depleted in incompatible elements. E-MORB: slightly enriched.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In the water table fluctuation method, groundwater recharge is estimated using:
options: Uses the drawdown of a pumping well to estimate specific storage
Applies the Theis equation to recovery data for aquifer parameters
Uses the steady state flow formula of Thiem for two wells
questions.solution: WTF: water table rise from precipitation. S_y from specific yield tests.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Crystal symmetry elements: rotation axes, mirror planes, inversion centers:
options: 14 groups. Symmetry combinations define the fourteen Bravais lattice types
Combination defines point group (32 crystallographic point groups)
7 groups. Each symmetry combination corresponds to one of the seven crystal systems
230 groups. The combinations yield every possible space group for minerals
questions.solution: Point group: symmetry operations. Space group: point group + translations = 230 groups.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A dipping coal seam outcrops over a horizontal width of 80 m on flat ground and dips at 20°. Its true thickness is about:
questions.solution: True thickness = horizontal width × sin(dip) = 80×sin20° ≈ 27.36 m.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: From the surface inward, the major layers of the Earth are:
questions.solution: The Earth is layered into a thin crust, a thick mantle, and a metallic core.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Plagioclase feldspar typically shows which common type of twinning?
options: Occurs only in very slowly cooled plutonic rocks
Simple Carlsbad twinning on a single crystal scale
Twinning restricted to adjacent grains at grain contacts
questions.solution: Plagioclase: polysynthetic twinning. Causes striations.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Radiocarbon (C-14) dating is applicable to organic material up to what maximum age, and what does it require?
options: ¹⁴C (T½ = 5730 yr). For organic material <50 ka. Atmospheric production, calibration curve
U-Pb method applied to zircon crystals extracted from the same strata body being studied, for ancient rocks
Rb-Sr method applied to whole-rock samples of the basement crystalline rocks below
K-Ar method applied to potassium minerals of the volcanic ash beds that are present
questions.solution: C-14: radiocarbon. β⁻ decay. Libby (1949). Calibration: tree rings, corals, speleothems.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Geotechnical investigation borehole spacing depends on:
options: Only the overall height of the proposed structure
Only the financial budget allocated for the work
No fixed rule exists, spacing is purely arbitrary
questions.solution: Borehole spacing: simple terrain large structures ~30-50m. Complex terrain small structures ~5-15m. BS 5930 guidance.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Seismic P-wave velocity in rocks generally increases with which rock properties?
options: Increasing rock density and elastic modulus
Increasing porosity filled with low density fluids
Decreasing temperature and increasing pore pressure
Decreasing density while shear modulus constant
questions.solution: P-wave: Vp = sqrt((K+4/3G)/ρ). Higher density and modulus = higher velocity. Porosity decreases velocity.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The dip direction of cross-bedding in a sandstone bed indicates which direction?
options: Paleo-water depth at time of deposition
Relative age of the sedimentary unit
questions.solution: Cross-bedding: foresets dip in flow direction. Used for paleocurrent analysis. Restores paleogeography.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Diagenetic environment — meteoric phreatic:
options: Zone above the water table in the vadose zone, where only gravitational and meniscus cement forms between grains
Freshwater-saturated zone below water table. Equant/relict calcite cement. Dissolution common
Marine zone dominated by aragonite needle cement and micrite envelopes on all grains
Deep burial zone with pressure dissolution, stylolites and late ferroan calcite cement
questions.solution: Meteoric phreatic: stable isotopes (δ¹⁸O depleted). Vadose: meniscus, gravitational cement.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Lineation in metamorphic rocks indicates:
options: Trace of the axial plane of a fold
Dip direction of the dominant fault plane
questions.solution: Stretching lineation: alignment of elongate minerals. Indicates transport/stretching direction. Key kinematic indicator.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is a discordant tabular igneous intrusion that cross-cuts bedding?
options: Concordant sheet intrusion emplaced parallel to the bedding planes
Horizontal intrusion that lies parallel to stratification of the host rock
Concordant intrusion that domes the strata above its flat floor
questions.solution: Dyke: vertical or steeply dipping. Radiating or linear swarms.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Ultrahigh Temperature (UHT) metamorphism:
options: >900°C at 7-13 kbar. Sapphirine, orthopyroxene + sillimanite, osumilite. Lower crust
Eclogite facies metamorphism at pressures above 2.7 GPa during deep continental subduction
Blueschist facies conditions typical of cold subduction-zone environments at shallow mantle depths
Greenschist facies burial along a normal continental geothermal gradient at moderate crustal depths
questions.solution: UHT: peak T >900°C. Mg-Al granulites. Eastern Ghats, Napier Complex (Antarctica).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which classification approach first segments an image, then classifies segments using shape and texture instead of pixels?
options: Segment image → classify segments (not pixels). Shape, texture, context. eCognition
Classify each pixel independently, using the spectral values only and ignoring all spatial context
Apply band-ratio indices to the whole image, without performing any segmentation step at all
Use per-pixel classifiers only, while ignoring the shape, texture and spatial context
questions.solution: OBIA: multiresolution segmentation. Scale parameter. Feature space. Better than pixel for high-res.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A sequence boundary (SB) is a subaerial unconformity with its correlative conformity; a type 1 boundary differs from type 2 in that:
options: Condensed section with glauconite and pelagic sediment formed during the maximum flooding of the continental shelf
Subaerial unconformity + correlative conformity. Type 1 (Shelf exposed) vs Type 2 (shelf not exposed)
Maximum flooding surface marking the deepest water conditions
Transgressive surface recording the initial landward shift of the shoreline
questions.solution: SB: base-level fall. Vail et al. (1977). Exxon sequence stratigraphy. Lowstand fan.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The gem mineral topaz crystallizes in which one of the following crystal systems?
questions.solution: Topaz (Al2SiO4(F,OH)2) — orthorhombic. Hardness 8.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Gneiss, a high-grade metamorphic rock, is characteristically identified by which feature?
options: Vesicular holes formed by the escape of volcanic gases during eruption
Banding (segregation of light and dark minerals)
Abundant marine fossils preserved in a carbonate matrix
A glassy texture produced by the extremely rapid quenching of magma
questions.solution: Gneiss is a high-grade foliated rock showing compositional banding (gneissic foliation).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal seam covers 1 km², is 3 m thick, with density 1.3 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
questions.solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 1×10⁶ m²×3 m×1.3 t/m³ ≈ 3.9 Mt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Accretionary wedge: deformed sediments scraped off subducting plate:
options: Oceanic crust and upper mantle rocks emplaced onto land by obduction
High-grade metamorphic rocks brought up to the surface from great depth
Volcanic lava flows erupted along the convergent plate boundary
questions.solution: Accretion: prism of deformed sediment. Offscraping, underplating. Mélanges: blocks in matrix.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which textural features are diagnostic of debrites (debris flow deposits) in the rock record?
options: Matrix-supported, poorly sorted clasts showing normal grading throughout
Clast-supported, well-sorted, rounded clasts with abundant imbrication
Matrix-supported, poorly sorted, angular clasts, no grading
Well-sorted, laminated sand with symmetrical wave ripple cross-lamination
questions.solution: Debris flow: cohesive matrix support. High viscosity. Liquefied flow: fluid support.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How is the extinction angle of a mineral defined under crossed polars in thin section?
options: Not applicable to minerals that are studied in thin section preparations
Always 45° for every mineral regardless of orientation
Angle between cleavage and vibration direction under crossed polars
Always 90° in uniaxial minerals viewed along the optic axis
questions.solution: Straight extinction: 0°. Oblique: 0-45°. Symmetrical: angle to both cleavages.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Metamorphic rocks are formed by the action of which agents on pre-existing rocks?
options: Evaporation and precipitation of dissolved salts from sea water
Rapid cooling of molten lava at the Earth's surface
Heat and/or pressure on pre-existing rocks
Cementation and compaction of transported detrital grains
questions.solution: Metamorphism alters mineralogy and texture in the solid state under heat/pressure.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Calcareous nannofossils (coccoliths), typically under 30 µm and ranging from Cretaceous to Recent, are used for what?
options: Radiolaria. Siliceous nannoplankton (>30 µm) whose opaline tests are used chiefly in paleoceanographic reconstruction
Calcareous nannoplankton (<30 µm). Cretaceous-Recent. Biostratigraphy + paleoclimate. Emiliania huxleyi
Diatoms. Siliceous nannoplankton (<30 µm). Used chiefly for lacustrine and polar marine zonation
Foraminifera. Calcareous macrofossils (>2 mm). Zonation rests on benthic chamber morphology
questions.solution: Nannofossils: produced by haptophyte algae. Chalk. High-resolution zonation for Cretaceous-Tertiary.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which factors primarily control the changes that occur during metamorphism of a rock?
options: Temperature and pressure acting alone on the protolith
Only the length of time the rock spends at depth
Chemical composition of the protolith and weathering intensity
questions.solution: T drives reactions. P controls mineral density. Fluids catalyze reactions.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How are tsunamis most commonly generated, and at what magnitude do thrust-fault earthquakes trigger them?
options: Ocean wave from underwater earthquake (M>7, thrust fault). Velocity ~√(gh)
Giant tidal wave caused by the gravitational pull of the Moon and the Sun only
Slow surface current driven by wind and the Earth's rotation alone
Local storm surge generated by cyclonic winds blowing over the open sea
questions.solution: Tsunami: long wavelength (>100 km). Wave height increases in shallow water. Run-up.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Unit cell: smallest repeating unit. For cubic: a=b=c, α=β=γ=90°. Volume:
options: V = abc, where a, b and c are the three cell edges
V = a²c, valid for cubic and hexagonal lattices alike
V = a², giving the cell volume in square length units
questions.solution: Cubic: V=a³. Tetragonal: V=a²c. Orthorhombic: V=abc. Hexagonal: V=a²c·sin(60°).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The compound eyes of trilobites are unique among arthropods because they are made of what mineral?
options: Aragonite prisms arranged in a simple lens array
Silica spicules that form a single large biconvex lens
Chitinous lenses lacking any mineral reinforcement
questions.solution: Trilobite eyes: calcite lenses. Holochroal (many lenses) or schizochroal (fewer, larger lenses).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Cosmogenic nuclide exposure dating (¹⁰Be, ²⁶Al):
options: No relationship between the nuclide concentration and the duration of exposure at the surface is known to exist at all
Concentration varies randomly with time and altitude of the surface exposure
Lower concentration always means longer exposure to the surface at all sites
Nucleides produced by cosmic rays in surface rocks. Higher concentration = longer exposure
questions.solution: ¹⁰Be in quartz. Exposure age = N/(P×(1-e^{-λt})). For surfaces >100ka.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In geostatistics, kriging interpolation is best described as which type of estimator?
options: Simple arithmetic averaging of all sample grades falling within the block being estimated for the resource
Linear regression of grade against a single regional structural trend surface
Best linear unbiased estimator (BLUE). Uses variogram. Weighted average of neighbors
Random selection of the nearest sample value to represent the entire block grade
questions.solution: Kriging: minimize estimation variance. Weights from variogram. Ordinary: unknown mean. Simple: known mean.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An ore body of 1 Mt has an average metal grade of 3%. The contained metal is about:
questions.solution: Metal = tonnage × grade = 1 Mt × 3% = 30 thousand tonnes (kt).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Epithermal gold deposits are subdivided into which two classes based on their alteration and mineralogy?
options: Banded iron formation precipitated from stratified Precambrian seawater
Deep plutonic lode deposits formed at several kilometres depth in batholiths
Porphyry copper stockwork vein systems with potassic alteration and disseminated sulfide mineralization
Low sulfidation (quartz-adularia) vs high sulfidation (enargite). Hot springs. Au-Ag
questions.solution: Epithermal: <300°C, <1.5 km. Hishikari (Japan), Yanacocha (Peru). Bonanza grades.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Coal bed methane is stored in coal primarily by which mechanism, and how is it recovered?
options: Free gas occupying the interconnected pore porosity of conventional sandstone reservoir rocks trapped beneath structural and stratigraphic closures
Tight gas stored in low-permeability shale and carbonate source rocks
Methane adsorbed in coal matrix. Sweet spots: high rank, good permeability. Recovery: dewatering → desorption
Oil shale yielding liquid hydrocarbons through retorting of kerogen-rich strata
questions.solution: CBM: shallow (300-1500m). Proppantless fracturing. Coal rank: high-volatile bituminous best.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Volcanogenic massive sulfide deposits, formed by submarine volcanic exhalative activity, are enriched in which metals?
options: Lateritic enrichment of nickel and cobalt by intense tropical chemical weathering
Sedimentary exhalation of Zn-Pb-Ag brines into reducing anoxic rift basin waters on the ancient seafloor
Mechanical concentration of heavy resistant minerals by fluvial and beach processes
Cu-Zn-Pb ± Au-Ag. Submarine volcanic exhalative. Kuroko (Japan), Noranda, Kidd Creek
questions.solution: VMS: stratiform, lens-shaped. Stringer zone (feeder) + massive ore. Besshi, Cyprus, Kuroko types.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A rock retains 25% of its original parent isotope (half-life 1.3 Gyr). Its radiometric age is about:
questions.solution: 25% remaining ⇒ 2 half-lives ⇒ age = 2×1.3 = 2.6 Gyr.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: On the block diagram shown, the inclined bedding plane dips at 30°. The dip direction is, by definition:
options: Parallel to the strike, measured along the line of the bedding plane outcrop at the surface
Perpendicular to the strike, in the direction of steepest descent
Vertical regardless of the strike, so dip direction always points straight downward
Horizontal along the strike in whatever direction the bedding plane is gently inclined
questions.solution: Dip (here 30°) is measured perpendicular to strike, down the line of steepest slope of the plane.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 4% moisture, 25% volatile matter and 15% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
questions.solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (4+25+15) = 56%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Darcy's law for groundwater flow states that the discharge Q is equal to:
options: Q = K·i where K is the permeability and i is the hydraulic gradient alone
Q = i·A with i being the hydraulic gradient and A the cross sectional area of flow
Q = K·i·A. K = hydraulic conductivity, i = hydraulic gradient, A = area
Q = K·A where K is the hydraulic conductivity and A the area of flow
questions.solution: Darcy: laminar flow. Valid for Re < 10. K = k·ρ·g/μ (intrinsic permeability).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The most abundant group of rock-forming minerals in the Earth's crust is the:
questions.solution: Silicate minerals (feldspar, quartz, mica, etc.) dominate the crust.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the hypsometric curve and what its shape indicates about basin erosion stage?
options: Curve that plots the width of a river valley against its distance downstream measured from the headwater source region of the river
Curve that plots the total length of a river channel against its elevation above mean sea level measured at every kilometre along the channel course
Erosion stage (youth, mature, old). Area-altitude relationship. Young = convex (upper), old = concave (lower)
Curve that plots the volume of water discharge against the time of year at a gauging station along the river course
questions.solution: Hypsometry: integral = area under curve. High integral > 0.6 (youthful).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which remote sensing classification method uses training samples of known classes to classify all remaining pixels in an image?
options: Training samples (known classes) → classify rest of image. Maximum likelihood
Clustering of the pixels into groups, without using any analyst-defined training data at all
Automatic labelling of the pixels, using a set of predefined spectral thresholds values
A purely manual photo-interpretation of the image, with no training samples being used
questions.solution: Supervised: user-defined training areas. Unsupervised: algorithm clusters pixels. Hybrid approach common.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How does earthquake magnitude (energy) differ from intensity (observed damage) in reporting an event?
options: Magnitude measures damage while intensity measures the energy released
Both magnitude and intensity are identical scales of the same quantity
Intensity is measured only by instruments; magnitude is judged visually
questions.solution: Moment magnitude (Mw): most accurate. MMI: I (not felt) to XII (total destruction).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Bowen's reaction series: discontinuous branch (mafic minerals):
options: Olivine -> Pyroxene -> Amphibole -> Biotite (increasing silica content)
Fixed order of crystallisation that does not depend on temperature
Crystallisation of a single mineral phase throughout the cooling interval
Reverse order in which biotite crystallises before olivine at high temperature
questions.solution: Discontinuous: olivine (early, high T) to biotite (late, lower T). Continuous: Ca-plagioclase to Na-plagioclase.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What are the major subdivisions of the Siwalik Group and their representative formations?
options: Two divisions, an older marine shelf unit and a younger deltaic unit of the foredeep basin margin
Lower (Kamliyal), Middle (Nagri, Dhok Pathan), Upper (Tatrot, Pinjor, Boulder Conglomerate)
Five divisions based entirely on the changing grain size of the conglomerates present
Four divisions of equal thickness defined on the basis of cyclic bedding repetition
questions.solution: Siwalik: molasse (Himalayan erosion). Hominoid fossils (Ramapithecus). Thickness >5000m.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In carbonate diagenesis, what does neomorphism refer to, and what is its typical outcome?
options: Replacement of limestone by microcrystalline quartz derived from biogenic silica during early burial diagenesis
Replacement of aragonite or calcite by calcite of different crystal size (aggrading neomorphism)
Complete dissolution of carbonate minerals followed by precipitation of new blocky calcite in all pores
Replacement of calcite by dolomite in magnesium-rich brines during shallow burial diagenesis
questions.solution: Neomorphism: wet transformation. Microspar → pseudospar. Aragonite → calcite inversion.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Contact (thermal) metamorphism is produced mainly by what, and where does it occur relative to an intrusion?
options: Regional pressure acting over an entire orogenic belt
Heat from intrusion. Aureole around pluton
Shock wave from a large meteorite impact event
Hot seawater circulation along mid-ocean ridges
questions.solution: Contact: high T, low P. Hornfels. Spotted slates near intrusion.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The fastest seismic body waves, which arrive first at a station, are:
questions.solution: P-waves are compressional and travel fastest, arriving before slower S and surface waves.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a variogram model, the sill and range represent which aspects of spatial variability?
options: Constant semivariance at all lags, implying no spatial correlation in the data
Semivariance vs distance. Sill = total variance. Range = correlation length
A linear semivariance increasing without bound, implying that no finite sill value exists
Semivariance that is undefined because the regionalized variable is purely random
questions.solution: Variogram: γ(h) = ½E[(Z(x)-Z(x+h))²]. Spherical, exponential, Gaussian models. Nugget effect.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A rock retains 50% of its original parent isotope (half-life 1.3 Gyr). Its radiometric age is about:
questions.solution: 50% remaining ⇒ 1 half-lives ⇒ age = 1×1.3 = 1.3 Gyr.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How does porosity typically differ between the core and the damage zone of a fault zone?
options: Core: low porosity (gouge). Damage zone: high fracture porosity. Conduit-barrier
The fault core is the most porous part and the damage zone acts as a sealing barrier to flow
Porosity increases steadily and monotonically from the protolith toward the fault core
The entire fault zone has uniform porosity equal to the undeformed host rock's porosity
questions.solution: Fault seal: clay smear, cataclasis. Juxtaposition seal. Membrane seal (capillary entry pressure).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which parameters are used to judge the quality of coal intended for coking?
options: Only the ash content of the raw coal as mined from the seam as it is produced
Moisture content and volatile matter alone in the as-received sample of the coal
Sulphur and phosphorus content of the coal as determined by ultimate analysis
Caking index (GRI), CRI (coke reactivity), CSR (coke strength after reaction)
questions.solution: Coking: GRI >70 for good coking. CRI <25, CSR >65 for blast furnace coke.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Transmissivity T = K*b. For K=10 m/day, aquifer thickness b=20m:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What hardness value does the mineral apatite possess on the Mohs scale of hardness?
questions.solution: Ca5(PO4)3(F,Cl,OH). Index mineral #5. Phosphate ore.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: U-shaped valleys, cirques, arêtes, horns, hanging valleys and moraines are landforms created by which agent?
options: Cone of sediment deposited where a mountain stream abruptly meets a plain at the foot of the mountain front
Narrow steep-sided valley produced by active river downcutting and vertical incision of the river bed
U-shaped valley, cirque, arête, horn, hanging valley, moraine (lateral, medial, terminal)
Sediment body deposited where a river enters a lake or sea and spreads out into the standing body of quiet water beyond
questions.solution: Glacial: erosion (U-valley) and deposition (moraine, drumlin, esker, till).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In GIS, landslide susceptibility mapping commonly uses a weighted overlay of which factors such as slope, geology, rainfall, and land use?
options: Analysis that uses a single factor only, such as the slope gradient being considered alone
Weighted overlay: slope, geology, rainfall, land use, distance to faults
The distance to rivers only, while ignoring the geology and land use factors entirely
Rainfall intensity that is recorded over just a single monsoon season period
questions.solution: Susceptibility: heuristic, statistical (logistic regression), deterministic (infinite slope). Machine learning.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Squeezing ground in a tunnel results from high stress acting on weak rock that deforms:
options: High stress in weak rock → plastic deformation. Invert struts needed
Rapid brittle failure of the rock mass with sudden and violent bursting
Continuous inflow of gas under high pressure from the tunnel face
High-permeability rock with steady seepage into the excavation
questions.solution: Squeezing: ductile deformation. Caused by high overburden, weak rock (shale).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Lamprophyre: volatile-rich, porphyritic mafic igneous rock. Phenocrysts typically:
options: Quartz and alkali feldspar set in a coarse-grained equigranular matrix
Amphibole, biotite, or olivine in fine groundmass
Only quartz phenocrysts in a groundmass free of ferromagnesian minerals
Plagioclase and sanidine phenocrysts in a glassy volcanic matrix
questions.solution: Lamprophyre: lamprophyric texture. Dark minerals as phenocrysts. Often associated with diamond pipes.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What does the principle of original horizontality state about the deposition of sediments?
options: Sediments always deposited inclined at the angle of repose of the grains
Sediments deposited in curved and wavy surfaces following the basin contours
Sediments deposited in near-vertical sheets along active fault scarps
questions.solution: Steno: tilted beds indicate post-depositional deformation.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The hornblende hornfels facies, a moderate-grade contact metamorphic facies, is characterized by which assemblage?
options: Contact metamorphism, moderate grade. Plagioclase + hornblende + cordierite
Low-grade contact metamorphism in which albite and epidote minerals remain stable
Regional metamorphism at high pressure typical of active subduction zones
Very high-grade contact metamorphism with pyroxene and no hydrous minerals remaining stable
questions.solution: Hornfels facies: pyroxene-hornfels (high), hornblende-hornfels (medium), albite-epidote (low).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An ore body of 5 Mt has an average metal grade of 1%. The contained metal is about:
questions.solution: Metal = tonnage × grade = 5 Mt × 1% = 50 thousand tonnes (kt).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal seam covers 5 km², is 3 m thick, with density 1.3 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
questions.solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 5×10⁶ m²×3 m×1.3 t/m³ ≈ 19.5 Mt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A mineral specimen of mass 78 g has a volume of 20 cm³. Its specific gravity is about:
questions.solution: SG = mass/volume = 78/20 = 3.9.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following measures is used to mitigate debris flows?
options: Contour bunding and terracing of the entire catchment area
Removing all vegetation to expose the source material
Check dams, deflection walls, sabo dams, early warning
Raising the channel bed with loose excavated spoil
questions.solution: Debris flow: high velocity mixture of soil, rock, water. Runout distance analysis.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How does a mudstone differ from a shale in terms of fissility and bedding?
options: Lithified mud (silt + clay). Massive, no fissility
Coarse-grained rock of well-rounded quartz sand with cross-bedding
Fissile mudrock that splits easily along bedding planes into thin sheets
Volcanic rock with a glassy texture formed by rapid cooling of lava
questions.solution: Mudstone vs shale: shale splits into thin layers (fissile).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Using a simplified proxy where calorific value ≈ 70 × fixed-carbon%, a coal with 40% fixed carbon has a calorific value of about:
questions.solution: CV ≈ 70 × 40 = 2800 kcal/kg (illustrative proxy).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which matrix and statistics, including the Kappa coefficient, are used to assess how accurately an image has been classified?
options: Reporting only a single overall accuracy percentage, without any per-class detail whatsoever being provided to the analyst
A simple visual comparison of the classified map with the original source imagery
Confusion matrix. Overall accuracy, producer's accuracy, user's accuracy. Kappa coefficient
Simply accepting the classification results, without performing any formal validation step whatsoever
questions.solution: Confusion matrix: errors of omission (producer's) and commission (user's). Kappa: chance-corrected agreement.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A bed dipping at 30° shows a width of 30 m across a horizontal surface. Its true (perpendicular) thickness is about:
questions.solution: True thickness = width × sin(dip) = 30×sin30° ≈ 15 m.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which geodetic technique can monitor crustal deformation with millimetre precision and track plate motion of a few centimetres per year?
options: Crustal deformation monitoring (mm precision). Plate motion ~cm/yr
Useful for navigation only, and is unsuitable for any scientific monitoring
Mapping of roads and property boundaries at the regional scales, nothing more
Photogrammetric mapping of the terrain, without using any ground-based receivers at all
questions.solution: GPS: continuous GPS stations. Earthquake cycle: interseismic, coseismic, postseismic deformation.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How does fault gouge thickness typically vary with fault displacement and depth?
options: Increases with displacement and decreases with depth
Decreases with displacement and increases with depth below the surface
Remains constant regardless of the amount of slip or the depth of burial
Increases with depth but is unaffected by the total accumulated displacement
questions.solution: Gouge thickness: t ∝ d^α (α≈0.5). Thicker at shallow depth (more brittle).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Rhyolite vs granite: same composition but:
options: Both rocks share the same texture because cooling rates are identical
Rhyolite is mafic while granite is felsic in bulk composition
Rhyolite: volcanic (fine-grained or glassy). Granite: plutonic (coarse-grained)
They differ in composition, rhyolite being richer in quartz and poorer in alkali
questions.solution: Rhyolite: volcanic equivalent of granite. Same bulk composition. Texture differs due to cooling rate.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The fold shown in cross-section (beds arch upward about the axial plane) is a(n):
questions.solution: Upward-arching limbs dipping away from the axis define an anticline (oldest beds in core).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In the Hvorslev method of slug test analysis, hydraulic conductivity K is estimated using:
options: K = r²·ln(L/R)/(2·L·T₀). T₀ = time for 37% recovery
K = Q/(2πT) for steady radial flow toward the pumping well
K = T/S from the ratio of transmissivity to storativity
K = Q·W(u)/s evaluated at the match point of a type curve
questions.solution: Hvorslev: for low-K formations. T₀ from semi-log plot of water level vs time.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 5% moisture, 30% volatile matter and 20% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
questions.solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (5+30+20) = 45%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Hydraulic conductivity of gravel vs clay:
questions.solution: Gravel: K = 10^2 to 10^4 m/day. Clay: 10^-9 to 10^-5.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: To extract 5 m³ of coal, 60 m³ of overburden must be removed. The stripping ratio is:
questions.solution: Stripping ratio = overburden/coal = 60/5 = 12 : 1.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A bed drops 10 m over a horizontal distance of 10 m. Its dip angle is about:
questions.solution: dip = tan⁻¹(rise/run) = tan⁻¹(10/10) ≈ 45°.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In which crystal system does the common mineral gypsum crystallize?
questions.solution: Gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) — monoclinic. Hardness 2. Used in plaster.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A perched water table forms when a low-permeability lens creates:
options: Local saturated zone above region water table due to low-permeability lens
The regional water table surface that lies within a low permeability rock basin
An unsaturated interval lying directly beneath the regional water table
The piezometric surface of a deeply buried confined aquifer system
questions.solution: Perched: clay lens creates local saturation. Limited yield. Shallow wells.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 8% moisture, 35% volatile matter and 15% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
questions.solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (8+35+15) = 42%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The GASP geobarometer, sensitive to pressure, is based on which net-transfer reaction?
options: Fe-Mg exchange between garnet and biotite giving an independent temperature estimate for the same rock
Grossular + Al₂SiO₅ + Quartz → Anorthite. Pressure-sensitive. Used with Grt-Bt thermometer
Aluminum saturation index of the bulk rock used to infer crystallization depth of the source magma
Si-content of phengite calibrated as a temperature-dependent barometer for low-grade pelitic schists
questions.solution: GASP: Ca transfer. K = a_An³/(a_Grs·a_Ky²·a_Qz). P from equilibrium constant.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: For a geological cross-section to be considered balanced, what condition must be satisfied during restoration?
options: Conservation of bed length alone, ignoring any changes in the area of individual layers
Uniform horizontal shortening applied equally to every layer in the section without pinning
Conservation of bed length and area during restoration
Restoration with gap formation permitted in the synclines and fold crests of the section
questions.solution: Balanced: no gaps or overlaps after restoration. Bed length and area preserved.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Basalt is best classified as which kind of igneous rock based on its texture and composition?
options: Coarse-grained intrusive rock rich in quartz and alkali feldspar
Chemical sedimentary rock precipitated from a saturated brine solution
High-grade metamorphic rock showing distinct compositional banding
questions.solution: Basalt is the fine-grained, dark, mafic rock formed from rapidly cooled lava.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A bed dipping at 30° shows a width of 40 m across a horizontal surface. Its true (perpendicular) thickness is about:
questions.solution: True thickness = width × sin(dip) = 40×sin30° ≈ 20 m.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In deformed layered sequences, the sausage-like segmentation of competent beds known as boudinage indicates which strain condition?
options: Dextral shear across the rock mass
Strike-slip displacement along a fault plane
questions.solution: Boudinage: layer stretched and broken into sausage-shaped blocks. Indicates extension along layering. Common in metamorphic rocks.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The width of a wave-cut platform is controlled primarily by the combined influence of which factors?
options: The width is controlled only by the rate of sea-level change
The width is controlled only by the rock resistance
The width is controlled only by the wave energy at the coast
Rate of sea-level change, rock resistance, wave energy
questions.solution: Platform: wider in weak rock, high wave energy, stable sea level. Narrow: resistant rock, rapid sea-level change.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 5% moisture, 35% volatile matter and 10% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
questions.solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (5+35+10) = 50%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Vitrinite reflectance Ro% rank indicator: Ro < 0.5% is:
options: High-volatile bituminous coal with strong caking
Semi-anthracite of very low volatile matter
questions.solution: Lignite: Ro<0.5%. Sub-bit: 0.5-0.6%. Bituminous: 0.6-2.0%. Anthracite: >2.0%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In sedimentary geology, what does the provenance of a sediment refer to?
options: The mechanism of sediment transport from source to the basin of deposition
Source area of sediments (composition, age, tectonic setting)
The environment in which sediments are deposited and later lithified into rock
Post-depositional changes including compaction, cementation and dissolution of sediment
questions.solution: Provenance: heavy mineral analysis, zircon U-Pb dating, paleocurrents.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the main advantage of Ar-Ar dating compared with the conventional K-Ar method?
options: Produces results much faster in the laboratory than the conventional K-Ar method on the same mineral separates
Single heating step or step heating for age spectrum. No need for separate K measurement
Considerably cheaper to run on bulk samples of the same rock that is being dated
More accurate ages for carbonate sediments and their cements in the section
questions.solution: Ar-Ar: irradiation converts ³⁹K to ³⁹Ar. Step heating: age spectrum. Plateau age = undisturbed.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A P-wave travels at 8 km/s and arrives 20 s after the earthquake. The (approx.) distance to the source is:
questions.solution: distance = velocity × time = 8×20 = 160 km.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: To extract 15 m³ of coal, 45 m³ of overburden must be removed. The stripping ratio is:
questions.solution: Stripping ratio = overburden/coal = 45/15 = 3 : 1.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which logging techniques are used to determine in-situ rock properties in boreholes?
options: Gamma, resistivity, SP, caliper, sonic logging. In-situ rock properties
Only the measurement of core recovery and RQD from the recovered drill core
Only water level measurement in the borehole after completion
Geophysical profiling along the ground surface above the borehole
questions.solution: Well logging: lithology, porosity, density, water quality. Acoustic televiewer: fractures.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which geophysical method offers high resolution but limited shallow depth penetration?
options: Ground penetrating radar. High resolution, shallow (<10m)
Electromagnetic sounding for deep crustal studies beyond 100 m depth
Gravity profiling to detect large density contrasts in the bedrock
Seismic refraction using hammer sources for deep oil exploration
questions.solution: GPR: electromagnetic waves. Utility detection, void mapping, archaeology.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Seismic refraction — critical refraction:
options: Direct arrival that travels entirely within the surface layer after reflection at the boundary
Wave reflected from the interface returned to the surface at an angle equal to the incident angle
Surface wave travelling along the ground with velocity independent of layer properties
Head wave at critical angle (sin i_c = V₁/V₂). Refractor velocity V₂ from intercept time
questions.solution: Refraction: first arrivals. Crossover distance. Layer thickness: h = (x_c/2)√((V₂-V₁)/(V₂+V₁)).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Groundwater occurrence in hard rock terrains is primarily controlled by:
options: Water in hard rocks occurs only within primary intergranular pores between mineral grains
Fracture-controlled. Weathered zone (shallow) + fractured zone (deeper). Yield variable
The rock mass behaves as a porous medium with a uniform and very high storage capacity
Yield is uniform everywhere and entirely independent of the fracture network
questions.solution: Hard rock: only secondary porosity. Fracture zones, lineaments. High-yield wells along major fractures.

questions.stem: Goldschmidt's geochemical classification of elements groups Cu, Pb and Zn predominantly into which class?
options: Siderophile (Fe-loving, concentrated in the metallic core)
questions.solution: Goldschmidt's classes: lithophile (Si, Al, K), siderophile (Fe, Ni, Au), chalcophile (Cu, Pb, Zn, S) and atmophile (N, noble gases). Chalcophiles concentrate in sulfide phases.
